messages.content: For paper 1910.07154: What baseline did they use?

claims.text: To show the effectiveness of the approach, the paper compares the label accuracy of the "SUPPORTS" label against a supervised approach called HexaF.
Results indicate that their unsupervised approach is comparable to HexaF for the threshold φ = 0.76.
The system's results are also compared against two different classification thresholds, φ = 0.76 and φ = 0.67.

messages.content: For paper 2004.00809: Do they authors offer a hypothesis for why Twitter data makes better predictions about the inventory of languages used in each country?

claims.text: The paper reports that Twitter data makes better predictions about the inventory of languages used in each country.
In cases where corpora do not represent all languages produced by local populations, Twitter has fewer missing languages.
The authors state that Twitter provides a better representation of North America and Oceania.
The authors note that English and Spanish are very common on Twitter, so countries predominantly using these languages will have good representation by default.

The authors observe that Twitter data matches populations better when population numbers are weighted by GDP and worse when weighted by internet-usage statistics, implying Twitter represents more wealthy populations than web-crawled data, or alternatively that the Twitter collection was based on urban areas.
The paper notes there are more false positives in Twitter data, where the corpora suggest a language is used in a country but census data does not.
